answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each identity costly to mint: every agent bonds scarce collateral and must emit a steady work pulse that peers continuously attest. Spawning a crowd then costs like fracturing shale for one stubborn drop of oil — the economics drown you. A single honest node is cheap, but an ocean of clones is not, since each copy re-pays the full bond while its voting weight stays capped, so attacker cost rises linearly as influence flattens.
